doc.title: Vincent Pelote interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 25, 2017

chapter: Rutgers and the Institute of Jazz Studies
title: Lester Young's saxophone and Eddie Condon's guitar
summary: The coolest items in the Institute's collection are Lester Young's tenor and Condon's four-string guitar; they discuss Prez on The Sound of Jazz.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: What is the coolest thing in the collection, as far as you’re concerned?
As far as I’m concerned, oh God. There’s just so many things. I mean but I guess I’d have to say the coolest thing is Lester Young’s tenor saxophone.
That’s what I would have said. Because I was only there the one time but, oh look —

Yeah. There’s something magical about it. And I just look at it and I can see him holding it, that weird way he held the sax and everything, and those beautiful sounds coming out of that horn man. And I’m not even a horn player man, but I appreciate Prez man.
I love that moment that they captured on “The Sound of Jazz” with Lester and Billie.
And Billie. The face on her when he’s playing that solo. I mean she’s just like —
Just about a month ago I finally sat down and tried to write out his solo.
You know, and compared to doing some transcriptions it’s not that hard. But it’s so perfect.

Yeah. It’s just amazing. I remember you showed the film when you asked somebody what do they think about when they improvise – I think it was Bill Charlap. And you know, his answer was actually perfect. I mean I guess you really don’t sit down thinking all right I’m going to go from a C7 now to, I’ve got to make the third go here. Because how can you? You can’t. Well you’re an improviser. You know. It’s just so ingrained in you, it’s like breathing I guess. And I guess that was Prez man. Beautiful music just came out of that horn, man. That’s great stuff. The other cool thing I would say, and this is because I am a guitarist, we have one of Eddie Condon’s guitars. It’s a four-string tenor guitar. And I just think that’s great, because I would have loved to have been in there when he was playing that thing.
